pages.text: Mila points at pictures of homes: apartment towers, small houses, and homes by water.
In a city, families may live in tall apartment buildings close to schools and shops.
In the countryside, some families live in houses with gardens and open space.
Near rivers, some homes are built on stilts to stay above high water.
In windy grasslands, round homes can help block strong wind.
Builders use local materials like wood, brick, stone, or packed earth.
Roofs, windows, and walls are designed for sun, rain, wind, or cold.
Inside every home, people make routines for meals, sleep, play, and care.
Mila learns that a home can look different, but love and safety matter most.
Before sleeping, she draws many homes and writes: every family belongs somewhere.
